1a1760c73df464eb.subject: Speech models in Ollama
1a1760c73df464eb.body:
https://ollama.com/blog/speech-models

 
Ollama now supports speech models on macOS, with support for Windows and Linux coming soon. The first speech model is Phonon
[https://ollama.com/library/phonon], a family of small, state-of-the-art text-to-speech (TTS) models from Gradium.
 

Download Ollama [https://ollama.com/download]

 
Once you download or upgrade Ollama to version 0.40.11, run a speech model:
 

ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama."

 
Choose from dozens of voices with --voice:
 

ollama run phonon --voice Hugh "Once upon a time, a little alpaca lived at the top of a very tall mountain."

 
Accelerated by MLX, Ollama runs Phonon 35% faster than the next fastest option on a MacBook Pro with M5 Max, with the same
accuracy as the reference implementation.
 

https://ollama.com/blog/speech-models

 
 
Apps can use it through the OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint. You can also pipe in a chat model’s reply and hear it as
it’s written:
 

ollama run gemma4 --hidethinking "Tell me a fun fact about owls in two sentences." | ollama run phonon

 
Hear the voices and learn more:
 * Listen to examples [https://ollama.com/blog/speech-models] on Ollama’s blog

 * Speech documentation [https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech]

 * Phonon [https://ollama.com/library/phonon] model page

1a17315ca0477fd5.subject: anthropic’s books leaked
1a17315ca0477fd5.body:
----------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/62fa30cc-bcc1-4bb1-b4d6-826b012caa14/Frame_2147225200__1_.jpg?t=1792811649)
Caption: 


--------------------

--------------------
———————————————————————————


--------------------
This was the week AI opened its credit card statement and went a bit pale. Meanwhile hackers figured out AI makes breaking in cheaper than a dinner out.

Grab a chai, **here's the whole week in five minutes.**


--------------------
# **The bill showed up**

**Meta had a great quarter and then lost $124B in a day.**

It spent $34.9B on infrastructure in three months, more than the $32.8B in cash its business generated, which is its first negative free cash flow quarter since the 2012 IPO. Its spending commitments now sit at [$825B](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-meta-meta-shares-getting-170153674.html), up from $700B in July, and the stock [closed down 7%](https://www.openingbelldailynews.com/p/meta-market-value-loss-oct-23-2026).

We've all had that month where the card bill beats the salary credit. Meta just had it with a lot more zeros.

———————————————————————————

**The chip stocks joined in on the same day.** 

Lam Research, who make chip-making machines, warned that supply constraints will carry into 2027, and the chip index [fell 6.72%](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/329406/20261023/chip-stocks-lose-200-billion-equipment-makers-warning-counters-nvidias-ai-optimism.htm) with all 30 of its stocks in the red.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d835d3cc-dd59-435b-bed0-afad48da383a/Frame_2147225189.jpg?t=1792819740)
Follow image link: (https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/openai-working-on-new-30b-raise-at-1-25t-valuation-ahead-of-ipo/)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

**And Anthropic's books leaked.** 

The WSJ saw its draft IPO filing showing [$16.3B in revenue](https://investinglive.com/stocks/anthropic-ipo-draft-shows-nearly-15-fold-revenue-jump-and-600-billion-in-compute-deals/) in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1B a year earlier. Anthropic declined to comment, and Bloomberg has reported it's aiming to [list as soon as mid-November](https://news.bgov.com/banking-law/anthropic-said-to-target-mega-ipo-before-thanksgiving-holiday).


--------------------
# **Hacking now comes with a budget plan**

**On Wednesday, PHP pushed emergency patches** for two flaws rated 9.2 out of 10. PHP runs roughly 70% of websites. Both bugs were found with AI: Calif [found the first one](https://thenextweb.com/news/php2shell-php-rce-ai-openai-wiz) with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, and Wiz found both separately using Gemini and GPT. Finland [switched its government websites off](https://yle.fi/a/74-20252600) until the fix landed.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a5ceb461-a039-4339-bd9f-224d62aa3399/Frame_2147225205.jpg?t=1792820164)
Follow image link: (https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/10/19/breaking-news/how-one-hacker-used-ai-agents-to-break-into-over-100-company-websites/)
Caption: 

**OpenAI's own agents went off-script again.** Late last week it disclosed [four more incidents](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/chatgpt/articles/openai-discloses-four-more-rogue-160535912.html) from June, including one agent that made an unauthorised crypto payment. Somewhere, a finance team is still asking who approved that.


--------------------
# **The rest of the week, on 2x speed**

**Claude will text you first now.** [Claude Duet](https://macrumors.com/2026/10/21/anthropic-claude-duet/) sends you a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps an eye on them through the day and asks before it sends or pays for anything. Waitlist only, US Pro and Max. 

Claire Vo [tested it](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/claude-duet-is-beautiful-i-still) for Lenny's Newsletter, called it the most polished agent launch she's seen, and then forgot to use it, which is the most relatable AI review I've read all year.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5096198e-8961-433d-bca9-591fd87e2345/Frame_2147225206.jpg?t=1792820507)
Follow image link: (https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/20/chatgpt-now-lets-you-lock-your-chats/)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

**ChatGPT Ads reached** [26 more countries](https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/openai-expands-chatgpt-ads-to-26-new-countries/), and OpenAI says over 100,000 advertisers have already run campaigns. Your chats now come with commercial breaks in a lot more places.

———————————————————————————

**Builders, heads-up.** Claude's [new API version](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21) throws an error if you send temperature, top_p or top_k, so check your code before you hit update.

———————————————————————————

**Lawyers had a great week too.** AI picked up 8 copyright suits in one week, a [record](https://chatgptiseatingtheworld.com/2026/10/22/ai-copyright-wars-escalate-8-cases-this-week-sets-record-suno-anthropic-hit-with-yet-another-music-lawsuit/). Plus, [292 authors](https://chatgptiseatingtheworld.com/2026/10/20/after-filing-5-near-identical-suits-for-292-book-authors-v-meta-plaintiffs-firms-say-total-will-reach-1000-plaintiffs-new-strategy-in-ai-copyright-wars-who-needs-class-actions/) sued Meta individually and Canada's biggest newspapers [sued Anthropic](https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/news-publishers-launch-copyright-suit-against-ai-company-anthropic-in-ontario/).

———————————————————————————

**The US wants to keep American money out of Chinese AI.** Treasury [proposed rules](https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/206/Fact-Sheet-FAQs-COINS-Act-NPRM.pdf) to ban or flag US investment in AI, chips and quantum in China and a few other countries, with comments open till Dec 7.

———————————————————————————

**Closer home,** Jio Platforms' [₹30,213 crore IPO](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/companies/news/jio-platforms-ipo-anchor-investor-quota-nearly-30-times-oversubscribed-126101900538_1.html) closed on Friday. Infosys said AI is now [10.5% of its revenue](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000042/exv99w02.htm), and in the same breath cut its full-year growth forecast to 1 to 2%.


--------------------
# **Quick hits**

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is out under an MIT licence / MiniMax M3.1 Flash costs $0.15 per million input tokens / Canva launched [its first image model](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/canva-releases-its-first-image-generation-model/) / Microsoft's diagnosis AI [solved 83%](https://www.unite.ai/microsoft-diagnostic-ai-outperforms-generalist-physicians-in-science-study/) of hard medical cases vs 36% for general doctors / Nvidia is packing whole AI factories into [modular containers](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/gtc-berlin-2026-keynote/) / Arc browser [shuts down on Dec 22](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/arc-browser-sunsets-december-22-as-the-browser-company-doubles-down-on-dia/) (pour one out, Arc fans)


--------------------
# **Coming up next week**

* Claude's auto mode becomes the default for Pro, Max and Team users, so expect fewer "approve this step?" pop-ups

* OpenAI wants its $30B round signed by the end of the week

* DeepSeek's search API stays free inside Claude Code and Codex till Oct 31

* Notion agents move to monthly credits on Nov 2

* MeitY's AI regulation paper, promised "within a month" on Oct 8, is now due


--------------------
# **My Take**

Zoom out and the week had a funny shape. Building AI keeps getting pricier, with $825B committed at Meta alone, while misusing it has dropped to about $50 a site.

Even Sam Altman [told Stanford students](https://gizmodo.com/sam-altman-i-no-longer-think-were-gonna-be-able-to-just-patch-all-the-bugs-2000829947) this week that he no longer thinks we can just patch all the bugs. Which brings me to one small, boring thing worth doing today.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cd2d716c-d9a4-4df6-9aa9-77319b855573/Frame_2147225207.jpg?t=1792821024)
Caption: 

And hit reply with your poll answer, I want to know how many of you would let Duet text you first.

**Until next time,**
**Vaibhav** 🤝🏻
